newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Kaptol Banka sets up open investment fund.
newsitem.headline: Croat Kaptol Banka sets up open investment fund.

text.p: Croatia's private Kaptol Banka, partly owned by President Franjo Tudjman's grandson Dejan Kosutic, on Monday inauguarated the country's first open investment fund.
The fund Kaptol Proinvest will be dealing in both securities and short-term loans, and is also intended to have some real estate operations, officials told a presentation.
"This is the first investment fund... and we want to be even more profitable than our bank," said Kosutic, the bank's board president and one of the major shareholders.
He said the targeted investors would be private individuals and companies. Minimum investment is 1,000 kuna.
The fund's portfolio would be dispersed between 20-40 percent government bonds and central bank bills and some 10-30 percent shares and corporate bonds.
Some 20-49 percent would be accounted by short term money placements and up to 10 percent in real estate.
Kaptol Banka also plans to found a life-insurance company and another fund that would absorb vouchers from a proposed mass privatisation scheme. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
